meta.description: Corp — FLAT brownfield AD state (pre-tiering). The graph models who can log on where today, the privileged-group rosters, and the single attack path (PATH-001) that works BECAUSE a Domain Admin logs on interactively to a Tier-2 workstation. This is the t=0 baseline the migration migrates AWAY from. Reuses the Module 02 domain and the Module 08 PATH-001 fixture.

tiers.model: Microsoft tiered-admin (Tier 0 = identity/DC, Tier 1 = servers, Tier 2 = workstations)
tiers.note: This is the TARGET assignment from Module 11. In the flat state below NONE of it is enforced — Tier 0 accounts log on to Tier 2 hosts freely. Tiering = making the assignment real with Deny-logon rights + Protected Users.

hosts.name: JUMP01.CORP.LOCAL
hosts.role: Tier 0 privileged access workstation / jump host

logon_rights.comment: FLAT: a Domain Admin can log on interactively EVERYWHERE, including Tier 2 workstations. This is the brownfield sin — it makes the DA credential harvestable from any compromised workstation.

legitimate_work.comment: tallen's REAL job: administer the domain from the Tier 0 jump host. A correct migration must keep this working.

logon_rights.comment: A non-Tier-0 IT admin who legitimately works ON the Tier 2 workstations (helpdesk-style). Migration must NOT lock this account out of the pilot OU — only Tier 0 accounts are denied there.

GOTCHA the model misses: a service account that SILENTLY logs on INTERACTIVELY (it should run as a service, but ops wired it to log on locally on BACKUP01). A blanket Tier-1 Deny-interactive would break the nightly backup. The migration must spot this and exclude it / fix the service config first.
Ordinary Finance user — the attacker's entry point in PATH-001.
